newsitem.title: UK: Millions to enjoy Britain's Halifax windfalls.
newsitem.headline: Millions to enjoy Britain's Halifax windfalls.

text.p: Millions of Britons are set to enjoy hefty cash windfalls as the 144 year old Halifax Building Society joins the stock exchange Monday.
Some 7.6 million Halifax members will become shareholders in the flotation. Those who have decided to sell their shares immediately could pick up average windfalls of up to 2,300 pounds ($3,770).
Halifax's brokers Merrill Lynch and Cazenove auctioned 23 percent of its flotation shares Friday to institutional investors.

Analysts said this auction will have seen aggressive bidding from institutions which missed out on the strong early performance of another building society, the Alliance & Leicester, when it floated last month.
The result of the auction of almost 570 million shares will be announced Monday morning.
They believe the auction price could be between 650 and 720 pence per share, valuing the company at 18 billion pounds ($29.5 billion) and making it one of Britain's 10 largest.
Until now Halifax, like Britain's other building societies, has been owned by its savers and borrowers -- known as its members.
Last February, they voted in favour of a proposal for the society to convert to a public limited company and trade on the stock exchange.

Analysts say Halifax will be a leader in the financial services industry, with a profitable existing franchise and extensive capital reserves -- estimated at more than three billion pounds ($4.9 billion).
